notes.text: The opening continues a discussion by saying that the domain set, through its pi operation, defines a functor. The short canceled word remains doubtful. The added parenthesis and its long curved guide are preserved; the live verb is définit. This account reports the source construction without proving it.

The triangular diagram has Rev(Pi), pi-Ens and Ens as its objects. It labels the upper functor F and supplies two assignments from a variable E. The canceled vertical-arrow label is read via : tilde Pi, including a newly recovered colon. The relation graph at the left is reproduced as two vertical wavy strokes rather than assigned a new mathematical meaning.

The NB note says that the ring sign means the pi operations have been reversed to make pi act on the right. It literally opens with a square bracket and closes with a round parenthesis. Its short form dr and the point after op. remain as written.

The page then calls the functor commuting with arbitrary direct limits and asks for compatibility with an action on Rev(Pi). The actor letter is still Gamma/F, and the ink does not justify correcting it from the later gamma variable. The displayed isomorphisms and the following object condition, functoriality and transitivity are transcribed as source assertions, not independently proved. The displayed F has domain Rev(Pi) and codomain Ens; as typed, that functor is not itself the group acting on Pi. This makes Gamma the coherent actor reading, reinforced by the later gamma variable and the long middle bars of the page’s clear F letters. However, the disputed graph has an actual short low spur, and the preceding construction names its acting group G rather than explicitly defining Gamma here. These facts favor the first alternative without excluding a source slip F; no letter is silently corrected.
The final words are On trouve que cela signifie, with lowercase cela and no visible accent or final stop. The page ends there. Both pencil page numerals are recorded with their hand unnamed.

All source words, agreements and differences in C/H, cancellations, insertion attachment, diagram objects, arrow endpoints, indices, ring signs, primes, punctuation and pencil pagination were checked. No change to the accepted fragment is proposed.

The top insertion and its existing TikZ guide already preserve the visible word sequence and attachment. The thin guide crosses the f region of définit but does not cancel the verb. Both the opening canceled word and the diagram’s canceled via : tilde Pi label keep their distinct states.

The triangular diagram’s upper, upward and curved arrows have pointed heads; the two assignment arrows also have left mapsto bars. The relation next to the upward arrow consists of two vertical waves. The later displayed relation has a wave plus a lower bar. These distinct physical forms are preserved.

The NB literally opens with [ and closes with ). Its underline, action-ring sign, wording renversé les op. de pi, comma, and final short form à dr are retained. No normalization to matching brackets, digit zero, expanded droite, or trailing suspension points is made.

M0709 remains Gamma/F. Clear F graphs elsewhere have longer, higher middle bars, whereas the disputed actor’s spur is very short and low. This supports retaining the existing preferred alternative only provisionally. No independently contrary clear letter is replaced to obtain a coherent actor. The later gamma variable is not used to force the reading.

The object-condition operator cluster is retraced but remains readable as Ob Rev Pi. Its prime, membership sign and enclosing parentheses are preserved without inventing a deleted predecessor. All four primed Pi occurrences and both later gamma occurrences were checked separately.

The final line remains On trouve que cela signifie, with unaccented lowercase cela and no final stop. Both pencil page numbers, 13 and 25, remain attributed to an unnamed pencil hand. No continuation beyond this sheet is supplied.
